sections.html:
Medford anchors the Rogue Valley, roughly 27 miles from the Oregon-California line, and serves as Jackson County's seat. Estimated population on July 1, 2025 was 86,494, after a 2020 count of 85,824. No other Oregon city in the county comes close, and only seven in the state are bigger.

Roxy Ann Peak climbs to 3,576 feet beside the city. A foothill house and a valley-floor house deal with different slopes, drainage and fire exposure, so spell out the lot in your listing and not only the structure.

Only 56.3% of homes are owner-occupied, so Medford has plenty of tenants and plenty of landlords. A buyer looking at an investor-owned house will want the lease and rent history before anything else.

sections.h2: Wildfire history and what buyers ask
sections.html:
The Almeda fire began on the morning of September 8, 2020 and tore through the Rogue Valley in a matter of hours. More than 2,600 homes burned between Ashland, Talent, Phoenix and Medford, and one of the losses inside Medford was a mobile home park. Oregon has not recorded a more destructive wildfire.

If your house was rebuilt, repaired or ever touched by smoke or heat, expect questions about insurance, permits and value. Keep repair invoices, permit sign-offs and insurer letters in one folder.

ORS 308.146 lowers a property's maximum assessed value for the year when fire or another act of God cuts its real market value. A damaged house is worth a call to the Assessor's Office to ask whether that reduction was applied.

Lawmakers voted in 2025 to repeal the contested state wildfire hazard map that defensible space and building code rules had relied on. Separately, a 2023 law keeps insurers from using a state agency's hazard map to cancel, decline to renew or raise premiums on a homeowner policy.

Rogue Valley summers run hot and dry: an average of 61 afternoons above 90 degrees and 11 above 100. That kind of sun wears out roofing, exterior paint and cooling equipment, which are exactly the items an inspector writes up. If your roof or air conditioner is close to done, replace it before listing or be ready to concede some price.

The county bills Medford property tax. Call the Assessor's Office at 541-774-6059 or visit 10 S Oakdale Ave in Medford.

Oregon sets three payment dates: November 15, February 15 and May 15. Paying everything by November 15 takes 3% off, and paying two-thirds by then takes 2% off. Late balances collect interest at 1 1/3% per month.

At closing the tax year is split by days of ownership. You cover your share, the buyer covers the rest, and the title company shows the split on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Does Medford charge a transfer tax?
sections.html: Almost never. ORS 306.815 prohibits cities and counties from taxing real property transfers, apart from narrow carve-outs for rules that existed on March 31, 1997 or for low recording fees. Your title officer can confirm that nothing local applies to your sale.

• Every buyer who submits a written offer must get a signed seller disclosure statement, except in excluded sales such as an estate sold by a court-appointed personal representative.
  • Fire, smoke or heat history that an insurer or buyer could ask about.
  • Notice to tenants and a realistic move-out date if you rent the place out.
  • The current-year tax split.

Assemble these before the first showing and the contract phase moves faster.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
With no lender on the buyer's side, the appraisal and underwriting wait disappears. The sequence for a Medford house runs like this.

  1. Tell the buyer the address, what shape the house is in and when you need to be out.
  2. Get an offer and read every term in writing: who covers closing costs, whether the house sells as is, and the closing date.
  3. Open escrow at a title company, which checks for liens and back taxes.
  4. Sign, then receive your proceeds.

Cash buyers differ on how much repair they will absorb. Put two offers next to each other before choosing.

Overdue property tax stays attached to the house. It is paid from your sale proceeds at closing, along with the interest that has piled up at 1 1/3% per month. Request a payoff number from the title company at the start so you know what you will really walk away with. The Assessor's Office, 541-774-6059, can tell you what the county shows as unpaid.

sections.h2: What to bring to the title office
sections.html:
• Government photo ID, with your name matching the deed.
  • The latest property tax statement.
  • Your lender's name and loan number if a mortgage needs paying off.
  • Leases and deposit records for each tenant.
  • Keys, garage remotes, and papers for permits or warranties on past work.

Missing documents cause most of the small delays at closing. Collect them while offers are still being compared.

A title or escrow company runs the closing. You and the buyer sign, the buyer's funds land, and the deed gets recorded. Your payoff, any unpaid taxes and the tax split come out of the price, and the balance is yours. Since no lender sets a deadline in a cash deal, the date mostly follows your moving plans.

sections.h2: Selling a Medford rental with a tenant
sections.html: Plenty of buyers will take an occupied house, but the lease and notice rules stay in force for you until the sale closes. Find the lease, note its end date and the deposit held, and choose whether the buyer inherits the tenant or you hand over a vacant house. Settle that before you commit to a closing date, since a late move-out can push everything back.

sections.h2: Timeline from first call to keys
sections.html: The pace depends mostly on the title work. A clean title with no liens lets escrow move quickly, while an old lien, an unpaid tax balance or a name mismatch on the deed adds days. You control the part before the offer: have your documents on hand, answer questions the same day, and decide ahead of time whether you want to leave the house furnished or empty. Once escrow opens, the remaining steps are the title search, signing and recording.

sections.h2: If your house has fire or smoke history
sections.html: Write down what happened and what was done about it. A short summary with dates, the contractor or insurer involved and the permit numbers will answer most of what a buyer asks. Honest answers on the disclosure form protect you after the sale, and a buyer who sees clear records is less likely to push for a lower number later.

faqs.q: What county is Medford, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Jackson County, where it has been the seat since 1927. Direct property tax questions to the county Assessor's Office.

faqs.q: How many people live in Medford?
faqs.a: The July 1, 2025 estimate is 86,494. The 2020 count was 85,824.

faqs.q: Was Medford affected by the Almeda fire?
faqs.a: Yes. It started September 8, 2020 and destroyed over 2,600 homes across Ashland, Talent, Phoenix and Medford, among them a Medford mobile home park.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Jackson County?
faqs.a: November 15, February 15 and May 15. Paying the full bill by November 15 earns a 3% discount.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Medford rental with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers accept occupied houses. The lease and notice rules still apply, so check them before choosing a closing date.
